gemini.rationale: The transaction was a whole-company merger where OKSB's subsidiary, Bank SNB, transferred intact with its assets, deposits, operations, and employees. Because the product, processes, and organization all crossed the ownership boundary together as a continuing subsidiary at closing, there are no structural mismatches between T4/T5 or T5/T6.

grok.rationale: At closing, Bank SNB's customer-facing banking assets/deposits/products (T4) and its banking operations (T5) crossed together as the wholly owned bank subsidiary into the Simmons family, with only a disclosed later bank-charter consolidation timetable—not a product-without-process split—so gap_45=0. Operational processes remained housed in Bank SNB with rank-and-file retention expected and named-executive transition-period amendments to support integration, so processes did not transfer without the running organization alongside them at closing (gap_56=0).

openai.rationale: Bank SNB’s assets, deposits, customer-facing banking activities, and banking operations crossed together into the Simmons corporate family, while Bank SNB continued temporarily as a separate subsidiary, so no product-process mismatch was documented at closing. The slice states that most OKSB officers and employees were expected to be retained, while named executives had termination, replacement-employment, or transition-service arrangements supporting integration; thus organizational transfer was partial but coherently aligned with the transferred operations rather than structurally absent.
